paragraphs: On Wednesday, Teacher Kim's class talked about a lunch for Friday. "What would you like to eat?" asked Teacher Kim. "I have an idea," said Leo. "Pasta pancakes!" Teacher Kim wrote Leo's idea on the board. Mia looked at Leo. "What do you mean, Leo?" she asked. "I mean a pancake with pasta inside," said Leo. Everyone laughed.

"That's a funny idea," said May. "But I don't want to try it." "But a pancake is sweet, and pasta is not." "I like pasta with tomato sauce," said Lily. "Mom makes it on Sundays." "And I like pancakes with eggs," said Mia. "Why can't we have both?" asked Teacher Kim. "Some of you can bring pasta, and some can bring pancakes." "My mom can buy the tomatoes," said Lily. "My dad can buy the eggs," said May.

On Friday, the classroom was full of good food. There was hot pasta with red sauce on the big table. There were pancakes on a white plate. "I'm hungry!" said Leo. He took a pancake and some pasta. Then he put the pasta in the pancake. "Oh," said Leo. "It's not good." Everyone laughed again, and Leo laughed, too. "Now try them one by one," said Mia. Leo ate the pasta first, and then he ate the sweet pancake. "Both are very good!" he said. Teacher Kim sat with the children and ate pasta, too. The plates were empty, and everyone was happy.
text.summary: Teacher Kim's class talks about a lunch for Friday. Leo has a funny idea, and the children find a plan for everybody.
